reason: Developing red blood cells and haemoglobin building materials look like a direct way to prepare the oxygen-carrying cells.
expectation: The cells will make haemoglobin and become better prepared to carry oxygen.

alternatives.reason: These also look like they could make the liquid part of blood.

effect: The developing cells made haemoglobin and matured into red blood cells without nuclei. I can now prepare the liquid part of the sample.
reaction: The loss of the nucleus during maturation is interesting.
reason: Plasma water and plasma solutes look like the ingredients for the fluid part of blood.
expectation: They should form plasma for the blood sample.

alternatives.reason: I could examine oxygen binding first, but the sample still needs its fluid.

effect: The water and solutes formed plasma, so the fluid and red cells are ready to bring together.
reaction: The plasma picture makes the dissolved components easier to picture.
reason: Red blood cells belong in plasma, and combining them should advance the blood sample.
expectation: The red cells will be suspended in plasma as part of the blood sample.

alternatives.reason: I could try oxygen binding first, but the sample is not assembled yet.

effect: Red cells could not combine with plasma yet; the compatibility hint instead led to oxygen binding to haemoglobin. I can now try assembling the sample with the oxygen-bearing cells.
reaction: I was surprised that oxygen binding had to come before combining the cells with plasma.
reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells and plasma appear to be the next parts of the blood sample.
expectation: The oxygen-bearing cells should join the plasma as part of the sample.

alternatives.reason: These are also blood components, but I will try adding the oxygen carriers first.

effect: The oxygen-bearing red cells are now suspended in plasma, but the sample still lacks white cells and platelets.
reaction: The picture clearly shows what is missing.
reason: White cells and platelets are the remaining blood components shown for the sample.
expectation: They should complete the blood sample with its oxygen-carrying red cells.

effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood sample and the goal. The result also distinguished plasma carrying dissolved materials from red cells carrying much of the oxygen.
reaction: The final picture brought the separate blood components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: The oxygen-binding result was most worthwhile: it showed that haemoglobin can both pick up and release oxygen, especially where dissolved oxygen is low.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making plasma was straightforward but less revealing; it mostly confirmed that water and solutes form the fluid part of blood.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the game required oxygen binding before red cells could join plasma, even though my attempted pairing seemed sensible.

arbitrary.text: That required order felt arbitrary for assembling a blood sample. The hint supplied the oxygen pairing, but did not explain why the cells could not enter plasma first.

continue.text: I might continue to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers close to body cells, though this chapter's assembly choices were mostly predictable.
